instruction: Look up the final score of the 2017 Super Bowl.

metadata.explanation: Task variation for 2017 Super Bowl scores using slightly different phrasing ('Look up the final score'). Maintains identical complexity and number of steps as the original task. The user must navigate from NFL.com homepage to the 2017 Super Bowl scores page. The evaluator validates correct URL navigation using the existing is_expected_active_tab metric function.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies URL navigation to the 2017 Super Bowl scores page (https://www.nfl.com/scores/2017/post4)
Getter logic correctly extracts active tab URL from accessibility tree with proper prefix handling
Metric function correctly handles expected.type='rule' parameter - directly accesses rule['type'] and rule['url'] without incorrect nested access patterns
Data flow is correct: getter returns URL string, metric receives URL and rule dict, uses compare_urls() for robust comparison
Expected URL value is semantically correct for the 2017 Super Bowl (post4 = Super Bowl, 4th playoff round)
URL comparison uses compare_urls() utility which handles URL variations robustly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator only verifies URL navigation, not whether the user actually read/understood the score. However, this is acceptable for a navigation task where 'look up' can mean 'navigate to the page containing'.
Consider adding verification that the page actually loaded successfully (not just URL match), though this may be outside the scope of a simple navigation task.
